title: Cost Guardrails & Operator Playbook: Initiative for Batching, Caching, and Quantization
creator: Renee Martinez
description:
Summary: Create an operator-focused playbook and initiative tracker that standardizes how product and platform teams run cost-optimization experiments (batching, KV/prefix caching, model quantization profiles) and safely roll them into production. The playbook will include experiment templates, gating criteria, runbook commands for automated rollbacks, dashboards to monitor cost vs. quality, and rollout patterns for Dedicated/Private/Hosted environments.

Scope and goals:
- Define a single source-of-truth operator playbook for EconOps actions related to batching, caching, and quantization.
- Provide runbook steps for: feature-flagging changes, canary/A-B rollouts, emergency rollback, and customer-impact assessment.
- Build a reproducible experiment template: hypothesis, data slices, sample prompts, quality checks, acceptance metrics, and cost delta measurement.
- Ship dashboards and alerts for cost per token, tail latency, quality regression signal (prompt-set-based intent-match), and rollout health.
- Align with OKRs: reduce hosted token spend on non-latency-sensitive routes by 18% Y/Y while keeping user-facing quality regression <1% on monitored prompt sets.

Deliverables:
- Playbook doc (Confluence) with step-by-step operator commands and checklist.
- Experiment template (spreadsheet + JSON manifest for infra) for repeatable trials.
- Console dashboard tiles + alerting runbook.
- 3 field trials: smart-batching for low-cost routes, per-customer KV prefetch TTLs, and opportunistic FP16/int8 quantization profiles with safety nets.
- Postmortem template for any rollout that exceeds cost/quality thresholds.

Success criteria:
- One successful field trial per quarter with documented cost savings and no customer-visible regressions.
- Automated rollback triggers enabled for top 20 routes and tested in staging.
- Playbook adoption: at least three product teams reusing the experiment template in the first 90 days.

Stakeholders and owners:
- PM lead: Renee Martinez (owner of playbook scope and OKR tie-in)
- Eng lead: Priya Singh (runtime / batching owner)
- Observability: Marcus Holt (console dashboards)
- EconOps: Liaison - Ethan Cole (assignee for adoption & field trials)

Notes on scope limits: Private (air-gapped) customers will receive an audit-friendly version of the playbook without embedded SaaS links; dedicated infra changes that require hardware rebalancing are out-of-scope for phase 1 and tracked as separate ENG tickets.

risks: Quality regression: small but measurable declines on long-tail prompts; mitigated by prompt-set-based quality checks and canary gating.
Customer backlash: some enterprise customers may see fluctuating latency; plan to opt-in or provide per-customer override in Dedicated/Private.
Operational complexity: multiple knobs increase burden on SREs; include a simplified 'operator quick actions' subset in playbook.
experiment_plan: Hypothesis: Smart-batching + KV-prefetch + targeted quantization reduces token spend by >=15% on targeted routes without >1% drop in quality on monitored prompt sets.
Dataset: production-sampled prompt sets + labeled quality anchors (intent match) for each targeted route.
Metrics: token_cost_delta, intent_match_delta, tail_latency_p95, error_rate, rollback_triggered (boolean string).
Gating: automatic rollback on intent_match_delta > 1% or tail_latency_p95 increase > 20% for 15 minutes.
Rollout: staging -> 5% canary -> 25% A/B -> ramp to 100% if pass gates for 24 hours.
